body.x: Siemens AG President and CEO Roland Busch will deliver a keynote address at CES 2026, where he is expected to showcase the company’s full suite of industrial technologies developed to usher in an AI-ready era for manufacturing, infrastructure, and transportation. The presentation will emphasize how Siemens is merging the real and digital worlds using AI, digital twins, and automation to drive tangible, real-world impact.

The CTA confirmed the keynote, with CEO Gary Shapiro stating that Busch and Siemens are demonstrating how AI, when combined with domain know-how and data, can “reinvent entire industries” by streamlining design, planning, engineering, operations, and maintenance.

Roland Busch, who holds a doctorate in physics and has over 30 years at Siemens, drew a comparison between the current AI transition and the advent of electricity. “There was a world before AI, right now we are transitioning to a world that makes full use of it – including in factories, buildings, grids, and transportation,” Busch said.

He framed Siemens as the global leader in industrial AI—“AI for the real world”—by embedding intelligence into every machine, device, and piece of infrastructure. The company plans to show how it is leveraging its deep domain expertise and established customer trust to scale industrial AI from a “once-in-a-century opportunity into tangible benefits for industries and society.”

Under Busch’s leadership, Siemens was named to TIME’s 2025 World’s Best Companies list, a testament to its focus on industrial automation, future-proofed energy systems, and adaptive infrastructure designed to be more competitive, resilient, and sustainable.

At CES, Siemens plans to demonstrate its AI-powered technologies alongside its complementary ecosystem of partners and customers. The goal is to explain how its tech stack enables AI to scale reliably in industrial environments. This focus includes transforming manufacturing processes, making cities more livable through adaptive infrastructure, and enhancing the sustainability of transportation.

The keynote, which follows the CTA State of the Industry Address, is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. PST on Tuesday, January 6, 2026, in the Palazzo Ballroom at the Venetian. Busch will join a high-profile keynote lineup that includes leaders from AMD, Caterpillar, Havas, Lenovo, and Vivendi, as well as a live All-In interview with McKinsey and General Catalyst.

Visitors will also be able to experience the technology firsthand at the Las Vegas Convention Center North Hall (booth 8725), where Siemens will host its mobile experience center and livestream a series of interviews from a dedicated broadcast booth (booth 8011).
